referents.why: 'Him' (auton), object of 'crucify': Jesus, but Jesus is not among the candidates; the two offered (Pilate, Barabbas) cannot be what is crucified here
referents.category: object not offered as a candidate

referents.why: the imperative 'crucify' is said to the one who can order it: the crowd cries to Pilate, who has just asked them what to do; second singular fits Pilate

links.why: the shout is what they cried; the command is its content, not a role nested in it (R1)
'they cried out' is the saying clause and 'Crucify Him' is what is said (R1)

groups.why: the shouted command is the part and Pilate is the addressee; the crowd who shouted is not a candidate, so no sender is recorded

cant_tell.what: the sender of 'they cried out' (the crowd) and the object 'Him' (Jesus)
cant_tell.why: neither is offered as a candidate in this window: the crowd is named in 15.8 and 15.11, Jesus in 15.5, but neither is in the candidate list
